questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is correctly spelt. Select the correctly spelt word.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **frothiest**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Frothiest* - ***full of or covered with a mass of small bubbles__ *(*froth)*
 
• It is the **superlative **form of the adjective ***frothy***, meaning *composed of many __small air bubbles__ (froth)*

 

 * [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__***
 
• Degrees of comparisons of the adjective *'frothy'*:
 
 
• *Frothy *(Positive), *Frothier *(Comparative), *Frothiest *(Superlative)
 
 

**Thus the correct answer is Option 2**

questions.question:
**The question below consists of a set of labelled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

People used to preserve

A-companionship in absentia 

B- letters for years as these humble pieces 

C- of paper afforded
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **BCA**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph starts with ***'people used to preserve'****. *Hence the next sentence should say **what they used to preserve (noun)**
 
• **'A'**** **starts with the **noun** ***'******companionship'***, **'B' **starts with the **noun *'letters'***, and **'C' **starts with the **preposition *'of'***, it can be either **'A' **or **'B'**
 
• Among **'A' **and **'B'**, if we choose **'A'**, both the options **ACB **and **ABC **would render the paragraph grammatically absurd and structurally meaningless. This is because both **A-B **and **A-C **in this order** **are grammatically incompatible phrases 
 
• However, if we choose **'B'**, while the order **BAC** gives a grammatically erratic paragraph due to **B-A **in that order being grammatically incompatible phrases, the order **BCA **gives a grammatically and semantically coherent paragraph

**Thus the correct answer is: ***People used to preserve letters for years as these humble pieces of paper afforded companionship in absentia*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'no improvement'.**

The art of movement (has been), in complicated ways, culture-driven.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **no improvement**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• Auxiliary verbs like *is, am, are, was, were *that state a fact are grammatically incompatible with the past participle of the verb *'to be', *i.e., *been*
 
• This eliminates Options 2 and 3
 
• Option 1, *'have been', *is used to denote plural subjects and thus violates the subject-verb agreement
 
• *Been, *when used with the root verb '*has', *makes up the (**Singular)** **Present Perfect Tense **indicating something which has occurred as a phenomenon (here, *the art of movement *being *culture-driven*)** **

**Thus the correct sentence is: ***The art of movement has been, in complicated ways, culture-driven.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the idiom/phrase.**

Never-never land

options.text: An imaginary utopian place or situation.
A place that is worse than hell.
A place that you know that you will never be able to visit.
A popular place about which you have heard such stories that you would not like to go there.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **An imaginary utopian place or situation**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• An **idiom **is** **an expression whose meaning is different from the meanings of the individual words in it** **
 
• Let's look at some similar idioms as above and their respective meanings
 
 
 

 clean as a whistle
 place or person or thing that is immaculate
 
 

 hive of activity
 place where a lot is happening, and everyone present is busy doing something
 
 

 middle of nowhere
 place that is very remote, far from any city or town
 
 

 a den of iniquity
 a place where wrong and dirty things happen
 
 
 

 
 

 

**Thus the correct answer is Option 1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The word **'utopian'** means modelled on or aiming for a state in which everything is perfect; idealistic.

questions.solution:

**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice. **

The teacher should check the homework.

options.text: The homework should be checked by the teacher.
The homework is checked by the teacher.
The teacher is responsible for checking homework.
The homework will be checked by the teacher.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **The homework should be checked by the teacher**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• When changing from Active to Passive, the subject (*teacher*​) and object (*homework*) are interchanged
 
• The present form of the verb (*check*) is changed to past participle form (*be + checked*)
 
• The relation between the action and the doer is represented by the preposition *'by'*
 
• Thus the structure is: Object(the homework) + modal verb (should) + be + V3(checked) + by + subject (the teacher).

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

The whole biosphere, like

P : a chemically dynamic state

Q : the individual organisms that

R : live inside it, exists in
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **QRP**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• Clearly, a sentence does not end with a conjunction that or preposition in
 
• Hence, options 3 and 4 are eliminated
 
• Since the starting sentence starts with describing the noun *'biosphere' *and ends with the preposition like, it should be followed by a similar noun/pronoun

**Thus the correctly ordered sentence is: ***The whole biosphere, like the individual organisms that live inside it, exists in a chemically dynamic state*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word. **

Objective
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Prejudiced**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The word that is opposite in meaning to "Objective" is: Prejudiced
 
• "Objective" refers to being unbiased, impartial, or based on facts and evidence rather than personal opinions or prejudices. It indicates a neutral and fair approach to evaluating or assessing something.
 
• On the other hand, "Prejudiced" means having preconceived opinions or biases that may influence one's judgment or decision-making process. It signifies a lack of objectivity and fairness, as personal biases can cloud one's judgment.
 
• **Therefore, option 4) Prejudiced is the correct choice as it is opposite in meaning to "Objective."**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 

 
• **Fair**

 
 
• This option is not the opposite of "Objective." While fairness can be a desirable quality associated with objectivity, it does not inherently mean the opposite. One can be fair and objective at the same time.
 
 
 
• **Detached**
 
 
• This option is not the opposite of "Objective." "Detached" refers to being impartial or not emotionally involved, which can align with objectivity. Both detached and objective suggest a lack of personal bias or attachment to a particular outcome.
 
 
 
• **Straight**
 
 
• This option is not the opposite of "Objective." "Straight" typically refers to something that is direct, honest, or without deviation. It does not inherently represent the opposite of being objective.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

Many lost dogs ______ been given back to their owners.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **have**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Since subject 'dogs' is a plural noun, hence according to the sub-verb agreement, the plural verb should be used. Thus, options 2 & 3 are incorrect
 
• And, modal verb does not come directly with v3 form. Hence, option 4 is also incorrect. 

**Thus the correct sentence is: ***Many lost dogs **have **been given back to their owners.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be ﬁlled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

She does not agree, and ______ does Anita.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'neither'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• ***'Neither' ***as an **adverb**, is used to introduce a further negative statement, e.g., **"He didn't remember, and neither did I" **
 
• ***'Also' ***means *'in addition to'*. Using '**also' **here is grammatically incorrect as it is not negative in nature
 
• *'Even' *means *'including...'*. Using 'even' here is grammatically incorrect as it is not negative in nature
 
• ***'So' ***means *'thus, as a result,...'*. Using 'so' here is grammatically incorrect as it is not negative in nature and in fact, tends to give contradictory meaning

 

**Complete Sentence: ***She does not agree, and **neither **does Anita.*
